paper.title: Low-Rank Bandit Methods for High-Dimensional Dynamic Pricing

settings.name_in_paper: Low-rank dynamic pricing with known product features (or known feature span)
unmapped: Actions are price vectors in R^N (ball of radius r); loss R_t(p) = -<q_t,p> with demand q_t = U z_t - U V_t U^T p_t + eps_t, low-rank (rank d) structure through product-feature matrix U
Learner knows the product feature matrix U (or its column span)
Learner knows the bounds b on ||z_t|| and ||V_t||_op and the price radius r (used in tuning)
Adversary chooses z_t, V_t (V_t PSD) each round; demand noise eps_t i.i.d. mean-zero with finite variance
The demand vector q_t is also observed
settings.definition_quote: \mathbf{q}_t = \mathbf{U} \mathbf{z}_t - \mathbf{U} \mathbf{V}_t \mathbf{U}^T \mathbf{p}_t + \bm{\epsilon}_t ... we suppose $\mathbf{c}_t, \mathbf{B}_t$ may change every round and are possibly chosen adversarially.

settings.name_in_paper: Low-rank dynamic pricing with latent features and noisy demands
unmapped: Actions are price vectors in R^N (ball of radius r); loss R_t(p) = -<q_t,p> with demand q_t = U z_t - U V_t U^T p_t + eps_t, unknown orthogonal U of rank d
Learner observes the full demand vector q_t (used for online SVD to estimate span(U)) in addition to the scalar revenue
Learner knows the bounds b on ||z_t|| and ||V_t||_op and the price radius r (used in tuning)
Noise eps_t sub-Gaussian(sigma^2) with i.i.d. coordinates
settings.definition_quote: When the observed demands are noisy and span$(\mathbf{U})$ is unknown, we select prices using the \algsecondabbrev{} algorithm ... we assume the noise vectors $\bm{\epsilon}_t$ follow a sub-Gaussian distribution for each $t$.

settings.name_in_paper: Dynamic pricing with known features under general boundedness/Lipschitz conditions (A6)-(A9)
unmapped: Learner knows feature matrix U; projected feasible set U^T(S) contains a ball of radius r_down and is contained in a ball of radius r_up (known to learner)
Learner knows the bound B on |E R_t(p)| (used in tuning)
Price vectors in R^N, low-rank linear demand model

algorithms.name: OPOK (Online Pricing Optimization with Known Features)
Modified OPOK (prices p_t = U_hat x_t, U_hat with correct span)
OPOL (Online Pricing Optimization with Latent Features)

source.label: cor:knownu
source.quote: Under assumptions (A1)-(A5), if we choose $\eta = \frac{1}{b(1+d)\sqrt{T}}$, $\delta = T^{-1/4}\sqrt{\frac{d r^2 (1+r)}{9 r + 6}}$, $\alpha = \frac{\delta}{r}$, then there exists $C > 0$ such that for any $\mathbf{p} \in \mathcal{S}$: E[sum R_t(p_t) - sum R_t(p)] <= C br (r+1) T^{3/4} d^{1/2}

results.notes: Regret E over noise and algorithm randomness vs any fixed price p; independent of N.

symbols.Q: max{1, sigma^2 (2 sigma_1 + 1)/sigma_d^2}, with sigma_1, sigma_d the largest/smallest nonzero singular values of the averaged expected-demand matrix Q_bar^*

conditions: noise eps_t sub-Gaussian(sigma^2) with i.i.d. coordinates
tuning: eta, delta, alpha as in Theorem 1

source.label: thm:unknownspan
source.quote: For unknown $\mathbf{U}$, let $\mathbf{p}_1, \dots, \mathbf{p}_T$ be the prices selected by the \algsecondabbrev{} algorithm with $\eta, \delta, \alpha$ set as in Theorem 1. Suppose $\bm{\epsilon}_t$ follows a sub-Gaussian$(\sigma^2 )$ distribution and has statistically i.i.d. dimensions for each $t$. If (A1)-(A5) hold, then there exists ${C > 0}$ such that for any $\mathbf{p} \in \mathcal{S}$: ... \le C Q rb (4r + 1) d T^{3/4}

results.notes: Q depends on the singular values of an algorithm/adversary-dependent matrix; proof additionally assumes T divisible by d, T^{3/4} >= d >= 3, sigma >= 1 for convenience.

tuning: delta = T^{-1/4} sqrt(B d r_up r_down/(3(L r_down + B)))
